extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, compositors, and printers preparing manuscripts and setting type for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and rules for hyphenation, word divisions, footnotes, tables, spacing, indentation, heads, proofs, and manuscript preparation for printed publications. Covers typographic, editorial, and compositorial practices used by authors, editors, and printers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation of by- compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Compounds of "by-" should be hyphenated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: by-product, by-laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for co-, pre-, re- prefixes (vowel clash)
rubrics_metrics.description: The prefixes "co-", "pre-", and "re-" should take a hyphen when followed by the same vowel as that in which they terminate; ordinarily no hyphen when followed by a different vowel or a consonant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: co-operation, pre-empted, re-enter; but: coequal, coeducation, prearranged, reinstal; also exceptions for proper names, long/unusual formations, and cases where omission changes meaning (Pre-Raphaelite, re-formation vs reformation, re-cover = cover again). Note: some journals (Botanical Gazette) print cooperate, reenter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for negative particles un-, in-, a-
rubrics_metrics.description: The negative particles "un-", "in-", and "a-" do not usually require a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unmanly, undemocratic, inanimate, asymmetrical. Exceptions are rare/artificial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for non-
rubrics_metrics.description: The particle "non-" ordinarily calls for a hyphen, except in the commonest words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: non-aesthetic, non-subservient, non-contagious, non-ability, non-interference; but: nonage, nondescript, nonessential, nonsense, noncombatant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for quasi-
rubrics_metrics.description: "Quasi" prefixed to a noun or adjective requires a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: quasi-corporation, quasi-historical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for over- and under-
rubrics_metrics.description: "Over" and "under" prefixed to a word should not be followed by a hyphen, except in rare cases (e.g., lengthy words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: overbold, overemphasize, overweight, underfed, underestimate; but: over-soul, under-man, over-spiritualistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for Latin prepositional prefixes
rubrics_metrics.description: Latin prepositions "ante," "anti," "inter," "intra," "post," "sub," and "super" prefixed to a word do not ordinarily require a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: antedate, antechamber, antidote, international, suburban, superfine. Exceptions include: ante-bellum, ante-Nicene, anti-Semitic, inter-university, post-revolutionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation for extra/infra/supra/ultra
rubrics_metrics.description: "Extra," "infra," "supra," and "ultra" as a rule call for a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: extra-hazardous, infra-mundane, supra-temporal, ultra-conservative (but Ultramontane).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation in spelled-out fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: In fractional numbers spelled out, connect numerator and denominator with a hyphen, unless either already contains a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "two-thirds", "four and five-sevenths", "thirty-hundredths"; but: "thirty-one hundredths" (note also when not to hyphenate in constructions like "one half of his fortune...").

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphen indicating omitted common element
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more compound words occurring together share a component element that is omitted from all but the last word, indicate the omission by a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: English- and German-speaking countries; one-, five-, and ten-cent pieces; literary example showing fifth- and tenth-century Europe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphen to indicate incomplete prefix or suffix
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyphen is used to indicate a prefix or a suffix, as a particle or syllable, not complete in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the prefix a-; the German diminutive suffixes -chen and -kin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphen for syllabification
rubrics_metrics.description: A hyphen is employed to indicate the syllables of a word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: di-a-gram, pho-tog-ra-phy.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of everyday words that should be hyphenated
rubrics_metrics.description: Forty listed common words are recommended to be hyphenated and do not fall under other classifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: after-years, bas-relief, bee-line, bill-of-fare, birth-rate, blood-feud, common-sense, cross-reference, cross-section, field-work, folk-song, food-stuff, fountain-head, good-will, high-priest, horse-power, ice-cream, ill-health, man-of-war, object-lesson, page-proof, pay-roll, pay-roll, post-office, price-list, sea-level, sense-perception, son-in-law, subject-matter, terra-cotta, thought-process, title-page, trade-union, view-point, wave-length, well-being, well-nigh, will-power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary divisions of words
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid all unnecessary divisions (hyphenation at line breaks). Wherever consistent with good spacing, carry the whole word onto the next line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General admonition: prioritize good spacing over division rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dividing on two-letter syllables in wide measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not, in wide measures (20 ems or more), divide on a syllable of two letters if possible to avoid it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words of four letters should never be divided; words of five or six rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit consecutive lines ending in hyphen
rubrics_metrics.description: Never let more than two consecutive lines terminate in a hyphen, if at all avoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also avoid a broken word at the bottom of a recto page; next-to-last line should not end in a divided word; breakline should contain at least four letters in measures of 15 ems and up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not divide proper nouns
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not, in general, divide proper nouns, especially names of persons, unless absolutely necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid splitting names across lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not separate initials or abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not separate the initials of a name, nor such combinations as A. d., P.M., etc., into different lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep initial groups together on the same line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid separating divisional marks from the following section
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid separation of a divisional mark (e.g., (a) or (i)) in the middle of a sentence from the section it precedes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the mark attached to the text it introduces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide according to pronunciation (American system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide words by pronunciation, not by derivation (American system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: democ-racy (not demo-cracy); knowl-edge (not know-ledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide etymologically when compatible
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide on etymological lines or according to derivation and meaning as far as compatible with pronunciation and good spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dis-pleasure is better than displeas-ure; school-master better than schoolmas-ter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not terminate a line in soft c, g, or j
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not end a line in a soft c or g, or in a j; escape the division entirely if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, divide pro-cess (not proc-ess), spa-cing (not spac-ing); present participles should carry -ing into next line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide on a vowel where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide on a vowel wherever practicable; when a vowel alone forms a syllable in the middle of a word, run it into the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: sepa-rate (not sep-arate), particu-lar (not partic-ular). Exceptions: words in -able and -ible should carry the vowel over into the next line (read-able, convert-ible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid additional hyphens in hyphenated compounds when dividing
rubrics_metrics.description: In hyphenated nouns and adjectives, avoid creating additional hyphens when dividing across lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: object-lesson (not object-les-son); fellow-being, not jel-low-being; poverty-stricken, not pov-erty-stricken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat diphthongs as one letter in division
rubrics_metrics.description: A coalition of two vowel-sounds into one (a diphthong) should be treated as one letter; avoid dividing such combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: people (avoid peo-ple), Caesar (avoid Cae-sar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carry t in derivatives when accent shifts
rubrics_metrics.description: In derivatives from words ending in t, in divisions the t should be carried into the next line with the suffix if the accent has been shifted; if the derivative retains the accent of the parent word, leave the t in the first line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: objec-tive (from ob'ject); deject-ive (from deject').

rubrics_metrics.name: Plural s does not justify new division
rubrics_metrics.description: The addition of a plural s, adding a new syllable to words ending in an s-sound, does not create a new excuse for dividing such words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: horses and circumstan-ces are impossible divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide adjectives in -ical on the i
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjectives in -ical should be divided on the i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: physi-cal (presented as phys-i-cal), not phys-ical or physic-al.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not divide the word 'nothing'
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not divide the word 'nothing' across lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition: do not divide noth-ing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote indices: use superior figures and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: For reference indices, as a rule, use superior figures; place index figures in the text after punctuation marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use asterisks/daggers in special cases (e.g., tables) where figures would cause confusion. Example placement: after punctuation enclosing quotations or sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of non-figure footnote symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: When figures are not used, the sequence of indices should be: * (asterisk), † (dagger), ‡ (double dagger), § (section mark), || (parallels), ¶ (paragraph mark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that order consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ibid., loc. cit., op. cit.
rubrics_metrics.description: Where references to the same work follow each other closely and uninterruptedly, use ibid. instead of repeating the title; ibid. stands in for as much of the previous reference as is repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ibid. should not ordinarily be used for the first footnote on a verso page; prefer repeating the short title or using loc. cit. or op. cit. Examples shown with Spencer references and ibid. usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit repeating author's name in footnote if in text
rubrics_metrics.description: If the author's name is given in the text in connection with a reference or quotation from his work, it should not be repeated in the footnote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example layout shown where an in-text attribution is followed by a shortened footnote reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place index figure after quotation marks for quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is better to place the index figure in the text after the quotation than before it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustration provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit abbreviations like 'Vol.', 'chap.', 'p.' ordinarily in references
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, omit 'Vol.', 'chap.', and 'p.' in references to particular passages; use Roman numerals for volumes, books, parts and divisions; Arabic numerals for Heft and text pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full terms only when confusion might arise; examples given for various bibliographic formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date placement in periodical references
rubrics_metrics.description: The date of publication in a reference to a periodical should immediately follow the volume number and be put in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow examples provided in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote numbering practice for linotype and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: In work set on the linotype machine, footnotes should be numbered consecutively through an article, or by chapters in a book, to save resetting; exceptions exist for some journals which use different styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note about linotype: changing a single number may force resetting of many lines; examples of journal-specific styles (Botanical Gazette, Astrophysical Journal, Classical Philology, etc.) are given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabular type sizes based on body type
rubrics_metrics.description: In 12-pt. and 10-pt. matter use 9-pt. leaded for open tables and 8-pt. solid for ruled; in 9-pt. matter use 8-pt. solid for both open and ruled; in 8-pt. matter open tables in 6-pt. leaded and ruled in 6-pt. solid; in 6-pt. matter both open and ruled set in 6-pt. solid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific point-size rules for tables according to the main text size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table captions and box-heads sizing and case
rubrics_metrics.description: Captions for columns of open tables and box-heads for ruled tables should ordinarily be set in 6-pt.; in ruled tables with multi-story box-heads, upper (primary) heads set in caps and small caps, lower (secondary) in caps and lower-case; where small caps used, the stub head should also be caps & small caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how to treat hierarchical table heads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing between table rules and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: In ruled tables there should be at least two leads' space between the horizontal rules and the matter inclosed, and, if practicable, at least the equivalent of an en-quad between vertical rules and contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure readable padding between rules and table contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of leaders in tables and columns
rubrics_metrics.description: In open tables set by hand, periods one em apart and aligned should be used between columns; when set on linotype, use regular leaders. In ruled tables, in the 'stub', leaders should usually be employed if there is room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use period or hyphen leaders; for columns of figures use leaders the width of the largest number; center the figures; if alignment imperfect leave more space on right than left.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading-matter alignment in table columns
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is reading-matter in table columns, it should be centered if possible; for lines that run over, use hanging indention and align all on the left.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hanging indentation for wrapped table text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: even picas and rule usage
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables and the individual columns in tables should be set to even picas or nonpareils if practicable. Double rules should be used at the top of all tables; vertical double rules only when table is doubled up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables with two columns should be open; three or more columns, ruled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table numbering and headline styling
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Table I,' etc., in headlines should ordinarily be set in caps of the type of the table body; the following descriptive line (if any) in caps and small caps of same type. A single descriptive headline (without number) may be set in straight small caps of the text type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on table headline typography and hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point system and pica standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The point is the underlying unit of typographical measures; the standard of measurement is the pica (12 points = one-sixth inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples showing lines set in 12-pt (pica), 11-pt (small pica), 10-pt (long primer), 9-pt (bourgeois), 8-pt (brevier), 7-pt (minion), 6-pt (nonpareil), 5-pt (pearl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type styles: roman, italic, bold-face
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinary type is called roman; sloping face is italic; heavy black face is bold-face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript indications: italics indicated by straight underline; bold by wave-line; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic anatomy terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of body of type (shank), face, kern, shoulder and font components (caps, small caps, lower-case).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications for manuscript markup: caps by three lines, small caps by two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and use of em, en, hair and other spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: An em (em-quad) is a square block used as spacing unit; en-quad is half an em; three-em, four-em, five-em spaces defined; hair-space thinner than 5-em.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples showing lines spaced with em-quads, en-quads, 3-em, 4-em, 5-em, hair-spacing; definition of em-dash and en-dash widths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Space evenly and standard interword/after-punctuation spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard line should have a 3-em space between words not separated by punctuation (and after commas); an en-quad after semicolons and colons followed by a lower-case; two 3-em spaces after colons followed by a capital; an em-quad after periods, exclamation and question points concluding a sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reducing spacing begin with commas and slanted letters; to increase begin with overlapping letters and straight-up letters in that order; maintain proportion of mostly 3-em spaces with at most an en-quad elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abrupt spacing contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not follow an exceptionally thin-spaced line with an exceptionally wide-spaced one, or vice versa, if avoidable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain visual consistency across adjacent lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hair-space or em-quad to avoid run-over
rubrics_metrics.description: Never hair-space, or em-quad, a line merely to avoid a run-over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid artificial spacing tricks that harm typography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not space out last line of paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not space out the last line of a paragraph allowing an em's or more indention at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unjustified visual gaps at paragraph ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short words spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Short words like 'a', 'an' should have the same space on each side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain uniform interword spacing irrespective of short words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use thin space after symbols and before certain abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a thin space after §, ¶, and similar signs; before 'f.', 'ff.', and metric symbols; and between 'A.M.', 'p.m.', 'A.D.', 'B.C.', 'i.e.', 'e.g.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: '§ 14. Be it further ordained...'; 'pp. 10 ff.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing in monetary amounts and measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In American and English sums of money no space is used between currency symbol and numerals; hair-space between s. and d. and the numerals in pre-decimal currency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: $2.75; £10 ss. 2d.; write measurement like 16 cm. with parentheses rules elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing after numerals at line beginnings and in headings
rubrics_metrics.description: After Arabic numerals at the beginning of lines denoting subsections use an en-quad; after Roman numerals two 3-em spaces. After Roman numerals in cap/cap-and-small-cap/small-cap center-heads use an em-quad. Small-cap headings should have an en-quad; cap-and-small-cap and cap headings two 3-em spaces between words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for visual spacing in numbered headings and centers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing for scripture passages and formulae
rubrics_metrics.description: Scripture passages should be spaced compactly as examples show (II Cor. 1:16-20; 2:5—3:12). In formulae put a thin space on each side of mathematical signs; between letters forming products and before superior figures indicating powers ordinarily no space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain conventional spacing in technical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indentation sizes by measure and point size
rubrics_metrics.description: For measures <10 picas indent all sizes 1 em. For 10–20 picas and 20–30 picas there are detailed indent recommendations by type size for plain and hanging paragraphs (e.g., in 10–20 picas, 12-pt/10-pt/9-pt/8-pt indent 1½ ems; 6-pt indent 2 ems; etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided table of indent sizes for plain paragraphs and hanging indentions according to measure and type size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry indentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In poetry center the longest line and govern indentation by that; when quotations from different poems vary slightly in line-length indent all alike; indent according to rhymes and length; in blank verse align lines; if consecutive lines rhyme align them; if rhymes alternate indent rhyming lines alike; indent disproportionately short lines more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and multiple stanza cases provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer plain paragraphs; use hanging indention for emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: In ordinary reading matter plain (regular) paragraphs are preferable; use hanging indention to bring out opening words, paragraph numbers, or long center-heads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hanging indention defined and its typical uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leads and slugs: definitions and standard sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: A lead is a strip of metal separating lines; ordinary standard lead is 2 points thick. A slug is thicker (standard sizes 6 and 12 points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matter with leads between lines is 'leaded'; without is 'solid'. Many books are leaded; index and certain paragraphs may be set solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Head/heading types and styling
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and styling rules for center-heads, side-heads, cut-in heads, box-heads, running-heads; center-heads usually set in caps or small caps; multi-line center-heads use pyramid or hanging indention; side-heads often in italics or caps-and-small-caps; running-heads two points smaller than text type and can give main title on verso and chapter title on recto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown and style recommendations for readability and hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph kinds: plain vs hanging
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds: plain paragraphs have first line indented and others flush; hanging paragraph has first line flush and others indented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition and usage contexts provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof types definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Galley-proof: impression of type in a galley; page-proof: impression of type material made up into page form; plate-proof/foundry-proof: proof taken before electrotype; foul proof: galley-proof with author's corrections; revise: new corrected proof from a marked proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct proof type names in production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up terms: folio, drop-folio, half-title
rubrics_metrics.description: Make-up is arranging type-lines into page form. Folio is page-number (even on verso, odd on recto); drop-folio is page-number at bottom. Half-title (bastard title) is abbreviated title on separate preceding page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit appropriate copy for title pages and prefaces etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typesetting machine descriptions (linotype, monotype)
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions of composing machines: linotype casts lines of type automatically from matrices; monotype punches perforations later cast each character separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand machine-specific implications for corrections and proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript preparation: general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be typewritten or in perfectly clear handwriting (typewritten preferable); sheets uniform size (9x11" desirable); use only one side of the paper; never roll manuscripts; place flat in box or envelope; sheets not fastened except by pins or clips; use mucilage (not pins) when fastening pieces together; leave liberal margins at top and left for reader/printer directions; pages numbered consecutively; inserted/omitted pages clearly indicated (4A, 4B; omitted pages marked '4-7').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions for practical handling and physical organization of manuscript sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript additions and inserts labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Additions to original pages should be placed after the sheets to which they belong and marked 'Insert A', 'Insert B', etc.; places where they are to be inserted should be indicated in the margin of original pages ('Here insert A').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps compositor place inserts correctly during make-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph marking in manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs should be plainly indicated either by indenting the first line or by a ¶ mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear paragraph structure for compositors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote marking in manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes should be clearly designated, either by separating them from the text with a line or using different-color ink; the word in text carrying the note should be followed by a superior figure corresponding to the one preceding the note; footnotes should never be run into the text in manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes on numbering conventions and linotype implications: best to number consecutively through an article or by chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and proof-marking practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and return proofs promptly; when marking proofs use standard proofreaders' marks and do not invent a personal system; answer all queries in proofs carefully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays and errors result from not attending to proofs; standard marks referenced (see p.106).
